note.note:
Action Plan:
1. Schedule face-to-face clinic appointment within 4–5 days for otoscopic examination to exclude cerumen impaction or other external/middle ear pathology.
2. Clinician to message admin to arrange booking; patient to call the support team using the number placed in the visit notes to secure the appointment slot.
3. Provide and review tinnitus education resource (link to be added in the visit notes) prior to the in-person visit.
4. Safety net: If symptoms worsen or new concerns arise before the appointment, book another video appointment for review.
5. Ear care advice: Avoid inserting cotton buds/Q-tips into ears.
6. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Left-sided reduced hearing.
- History of present illness:
  - Left ear hearing difficulty for ~6 weeks; intermittent.
  - Left-sided ringing/tinnitus; patient notes that background sound (TV/music) seems to reduce/mask the ringing.
  - Intermittent mild dizziness/off-balance; no true spinning vertigo; minimal/no nausea.
  - No ear pain. No ear discharge. No fever reported.
  - Right ear seems normal.
  - Prior brief similar episode ~1 year ago lasting a couple of days.
- Past medical history: Not discussed.
- Surgical history: Not discussed.
- Medications: Not discussed.
- Allergies: Not discussed.
- Social history: Not discussed.
- Additional review:
  - Chest pain: Denied.
  - Palpitations: Not documented.
  - Ear itchiness: Not documented.
  - Denies use of cotton buds/Q-tips.

Objective:
- Encounter type: Video visit; no vitals recorded.
- Examination: No physical or otoscopic examination performed in this visit.
- Investigations: None obtained.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Left-sided hearing difficulty with unilateral tinnitus:
   - Assessment: Unilateral hearing impairment with tinnitus; need to exclude a conductive cause (e.g., cerumen impaction) before considering inner-ear etiologies.
   - Differential diagnosis (from DDx, consistent with transcript):
     • Cerumen impaction causing unilateral conductive hearing loss with tinnitus (Medium): Fits painless unilateral hearing reduction over weeks; requires otoscopy. Opposed by presence of intermittent dizziness and the masking effect by sound.  
     • Early/probable Ménière disease (Medium): Unilateral tinnitus, fluctuating hearing changes, episodic imbalance; less typical without true spinning vertigo or aural fullness.  
     • Eustachian tube dysfunction/otitis media with effusion (Low-Medium): Unilateral, painless hearing change with tinnitus; no URI/allergy/aural fullness reported.  
     • Vestibular schwannoma (Low-Medium): Unilateral hearing loss with tinnitus/imbalance; less likely given short 6-week course and younger age.  
     • Idiopathic unilateral sensorineural hearing loss (Low): Not sudden; no audiometry yet.
   - Investigations planned: Face-to-face otoscopic exam within 4–5 days to assess for wax or middle-ear pathology.
   - Treatment planned: Provide tinnitus education leaflet; avoid cotton buds; no medications initiated.
   - Referrals: None at this time; pending otoscopic findings.

2. Intermittent mild dizziness/off-balance (without true vertigo):
   - Assessment: Likely related to the left ear process; no red flags elicited during this visit.
   - Differential diagnosis (from DDx, consistent with transcript):
     • Early/probable Ménière disease (Medium).  
     • Viral cochleitis/labyrinthitis, mild (consideration; less likely without acute severe vertigo).  
     • Vestibular schwannoma (Low-Medium).
   - Investigations planned: To be reassessed during the upcoming in-person ear evaluation.
   - Treatment planned: Safety-net advice to rebook if symptoms worsen before the appointment.
   - Referrals: None at this time.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements: Past medical history, medications, allergies, surgical history, occupational/noise exposure history, social history, vitals, and otoscopic findings not recorded. Palpitations response and ear itchiness not documented.
- Conflicts: DDx summary states sound triggers tinnitus; transcript indicates TV/music alleviate/mask tinnitus — conflict noted. Name discrepancy noted once (clinician addressed patient as “John” though patient stated name “Jack Smith”).
- Transcript quality: Minor pauses/overlap; overall intelligible.
